name: pilot-v1-area-derived-block
sources: Thermal material/thickness and convection defaults follow external/hotspot/temperature.c:default_thermal_config, not template.config (which has different convection/material settings).

Spreader and sink sides are explicit pilot choices of 50 mm and 70 mm, enlarged from upstream defaults to accommodate area-derived multicore dies. These and all cooling parameters remain fixed across configurations.
Ambient temperature comes from experiment-startup.json. Silicon power is ROI-average Runtime Dynamic + Subthreshold Leakage + Gate Leakage, at the original McPAT reference temperature.
limitations: Pilot temperatures inherit all gem5-to-McPAT power/area approximations and McPAT timing warnings.

The floorplan is a deterministic area-derived surrogate, not a placed-and-routed CPU. Each core is split into core logic, L1I and L1D; shared L2 banks are separate blocks. Coarse blocks assume uniform power within each rectangle.

NoC routers/wires are lumped into one contiguous silicon-equivalent block and all memory controllers into one aggregate block. Physical routing, metal overlap and controller locations are not recovered from McPAT.

The die uses the sum of disjoint McPAT areas at unit area scale, with no added whitespace; aspect ratio is fixed. Placement/adjacency and die area can change with core count or width under the same layout rule.
Headline temperature is the maximum of modeled silicon block temperatures, excluding interface, spreader, sink and package nodes. Unresolved within-block hotspots are not measured.
Steady state assumes ROI-average power is applied indefinitely. It is not the temperature reached at the end of the short PARSEC ROI, and this flow does not reconstruct transient temperatures.
Cooling settings are assumptions, not a calibrated hardware package. Leakage remains fixed at McPAT's reference temperature with no thermal feedback, power gating or thermal throttling.
